newsitem.title: USA: Gentex sees margin improvement in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Gentex sees margin improvement in Q4.

text.p: Gentex Corp said Monday it expects its gross margins to improve in the fourth quarter, after certain start-up expenses incurred in the third quarter hurt margins during that period.

"Operations have shown steady gains and are expected to eventually return to normal. We believe that our gross margins have a good chance to show some improvement in the fourth quarter," Kenneth La Grand, executive vice president, said in a statement.
Earlier, Gentex reported third quarter earnings of $0.18 a share, up from $0.13 a year ago.
Gentex makes automatic dimming rearview mirrors and commercial fire protection products.

La Grand said start-up costs with a new mirror manufacturing facility in Zeeland and associated equipment moves, plus installation of a highly automated manufacturing line for a second-generation compass mirror products, had a somewhat greater effect on the company than originally planned. As a result, both the third quarter gross margin percentage and net income were affected.
He added the reorganization of the exterior mirror manufacturing area to make new wide-angle, aspheric exterior mirror products also contributed to higher costs.
Gentex expects to begin shipping those automatic-dimming mirrors for European vehicle models beginning late in the 1996 fourth quarter.

La Grand said that the start-up of production at the new mirror facility was relatively smooth, in spite of some higher than expected costs. Gentex was able to begin producing and shipping automatic-dimming mirrors on schedule to its customers for the 1997 model year.
He said that four production lines are running on two shifts in the new facility.

Unit shipments to customers in North America increased by 30 percent in the third quarter and by 43 percent for the first nine months of 1996 compared with the same 1995 periods. Fire Protection Product revenues increased 18 percent in the third quarter and 14 percent for the first nine months of 1996, compared with the same prior year periods.
